questions.stem: All of the following statements about gluconeogenesis are correct, EXCEPT:

options.label: A
options.text: Lactate from vigorous muscle activity can be used as a carbon source in gluconeogenesis

options.label: B
options.text: Glycerol formed during the hydrolysis of triacylglycerols is converted to glucose in gluconeogenesis

options.label: C
options.text: Lactate formed in red blood cells can be used as a carbon source in gluconeogenesis

options.label: D
options.text: Fatty acids formed during the hydrolysis of triacylglycerols can be used as a carbon source in gluconeogenesis

questions.answerText: Fatty acids formed during the hydrolysis of triacylglycerols can be used as a carbon source in gluconeogenesis
questions.solutionHtml:
Fatty acids formed during the hydrolysis of triacylglycerols can be used as a carbon source in gluconeogenesis

Option D:

  • Fatty acids are broken down by β-oxidation to acetyl-CoA.
  • But acetyl-CoA is cannot be used as a substrate for gluconeogenesis because acetyl CoA cannot be changed to pyruvate due to the irreversible nature of link reaction.
  • So, acetyl CoA is never glucogenic.


Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 180

questions.stem: Conditions of fasting/starvation lead to glycogen deprivation and activation of the process of gluconeogenesis to maintain blood glucose. The number of ATP required for the synthesis of 1 molecule of Glucose from 2 molecules of Lactate are:
questions.solutionHtml:
6
  • Conversion of 2 molecules of Lactate to 1 molecule of Glucose requires 6 ATPs (2 GTP & 4 ATP).
  • The table gives the various gluconeogenesis enzymes which require energy for their reaction:

Energy utilizing reactions of Gluconeogenesis

Enzyme involved

Net ATP Consumed

Pyruvate to Oxaloacetate

Pyruvate Carboxylase

1 ATP

Oxaloacetate to Phosphoenolpyruvate

Phosphoenolpyruvate Carboxykinase (PEPCK)

1GTP

3-Phosphoglycerate to 1,3 Bisphosphoglycerate

Phosphoglycerate Kinase

1 ATP

Total ATP consumed from all three reactions from 2 Pyruvates

(2 x 1) ATP + (2 x 1) GTP + (2 x 1) ATP = 4 ATP + 2 GTP

  • As lactate can be converted to pyruvate without the use of any ATP.
  • So, the total ATP consumed from 2 Lactate molecules to form glucose will be the same as pyruvate i.e. = 4 ATP + 2GTP = 6 ATP (as 2 GTP ~ 2 ATP)
  • Similarly, Total ATP consumed from 2 Alanine or 2 Lactate molecules = 4 ATP + 2GTP



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 182

questions.stem: All of the following are true about fructose-1-6-bisphosphatase, EXCEPT:

options.label: B
options.text: Fructose-2,6, bisphosphate is an allosteric activator of this enzyme

questions.answerText: Fructose-2,6, bisphosphate is an allosteric activator of this enzyme
questions.solutionHtml:
Fructose-2,6, bisphosphate is an allosteric activator of this enzyme

Fructose-2,6, bisphosphate

  • It is produced by the action of enzyme PFK-II on fructose 6-P in the presence of insulin in the fed state.
  • It is a potent allosteric activator of PFK-1 and increases glycolysis
  • It is also an allosteric inhibitor of fructose-1-6-bisphosphatase and acts by reducing its affinity for its substrate and hence decreasing gluconeogenesis (see fig).




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 186

questions.stem: In the fasting state, increased levels of alanine indicate:A. Increased breakdown of muscle proteinB. Decreased utilization for gluconeogenesisC. The leak of alanine through the plasma membraneD. Increased uptake of alanine by the liver for gluconeogenesisE. Decreased breakdown of muscle proteinSelect the correct answer from given below code:-
questions.solutionHtml:
A, D

Options A, B, D, and E:

  • Each day, humans turn over 1% to 2% of their total body protein, principally muscle protein.
  • In fasting, after the depletion of glycogen reserves body starts utilizing stored fats as the main fuel but muscle protein breakdown is also increased for the utilization of amino acids and catabolic intermediates for energy and to meet the demand for increased gluconeogenic substrates for maintaining blood glucose for vital organs.
  • As a result of increased protein breakdown, ammonia is formed in the muscles which is mainly captured by α-ketoglutarate to form glutamate. Glutamate can also transfer some of its NH3 to pyruvate to form alanine in the reaction catalyzed by ALT.
  • This alanine is released from muscles which move to the liver via blood and is converted to glucose via pyruvate. The complete cycle is called as Glucose-alanine cycle or Cahil cycle.



Vasudevan Textbook of Biochemistry for Medical Students 6th Edition Page No. 105

questions.stem: Which of the following is the sequence of compartments of gluconeogenesis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Mitochondria → Cytoplasm → ER
  • The first step of gluconeogenesis (pyruvate to oxaloacetate by enzyme Pyruvate carboxylase) occurs in mitochondria
  • The next steps to the second last step (up to the formation of glucose 6-P) occurs in the cytoplasm
  • And the last step (glucose-6-P to glucose by enzyme glucose-6-phosphatase) occurs in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER).




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 182

questions.stem: Which of the following is most effective for gluconeogenesis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Acetyl-CoA activates Pyruvate carboxylase

Options B and C: Acetyl-CoA activates Pyruvate carboxylase

  • When OAA is used for gluconeogenesis in the fasting state, acetyl-CoA is not used up in TCA. So, acetyl-CoA accumulates.
  • Acetyl-CoA can never be converted to glucose. But it is an allosteric activator of pyruvate carboxylase, so, it activates the first step of gluconeogenesis by activating pyruvate carboxylase (See fig).
  • This reaction (pyruvate to OAA) is an anaplerotic reaction and replenishes TCA intermediate OAA.



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 182

questions.stem: Which of the following enzyme(s) is/are involved in gluconeogenesis:A. Pyruvate carboxylaseB. Phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase (PEPCK)C. Phosphofructokinase-1(PFK-1)D. Glucose 6-phosphataseE. Pyruvate dehydrogenaseSelect the correct answer from given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
A, B, and D

Options A, B, and D: Pyruvate carboxylase, Phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase (PEPCK), and Glucose 6-phosphatase

  • Most of the reactions of gluconeogenesis are reverse reactions of the glycolysis pathway except these:

Specific reactions of Gluconeogenesis

Enzyme involved

Pyruvate to Oxaloacetate

Pyruvate Carboxylase

Oxaloacetate to Phosphoenolpyruvate

PhosphoEnolPyruvate CarboxyKinase (PEPCK)

Fructose 1,6-bisphosphate to Fructose 6-phosphate

Fructose 1,6-bisphosphatase

Glucose 6-phosphate to Glucose

Glucose 6-phosphatase

  • These reactions bypass the three irreversible steps of glycolysis.
  • Other reactions and enzymes common to glycolysis and gluconeogenesis are:
    • Phosphohexose isomerase
    • Aldolase
    • Isomerase
    • Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase
    • Phosphoglycerate kinase
    • Phosphoglycerate mutase
    • Enolase



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 182

questions.stem: Which of the following substrates can't contribute to net gluconeogenesis in the mammalian liver?
questions.solutionHtml:
Palmitate
  • It is a fatty acid with 16 carbon atoms and is released from the hydrolysis of dietary or stored fats during fasting/starvation
  • It is broken down by β-oxidation to produce acetyl CoA as the end-product.
  • For acetyl CoA to be glucogenic it must be converted back to pyruvate by reversal of link reaction but link reaction is irreversible, so acetyl CoA cannot be converted back to pyruvate or we can say that FA, especially even chain FA, can never be a substrate of gluconeogenesis.
  • Hence, palmitate can't contribute to net gluconeogenesis in the mammalian liver



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 180

questions.stem: Which of the following is/are incorrect?

options.label: A
options.text: Fats can be converted to carbohydrates

options.label: B
options.text: Carbohydrates can be converted into fats

options.label: C
options.text: Glycerol can be converted to glucose

questions.answerText: Fats can be converted to carbohydrates
questions.solutionHtml:
Fats can be converted to carbohydrates
  • FAs are broken down by β-oxidation to produce acetyl-CoA as the end-product.
  • For acetyl-CoA to be glucogenic it must be converted back to pyruvate by reversal of link reaction, but link reaction is irreversible, so acetyl-CoA cannot be converted back to pyruvate.
  • So, we can say that FA, especially even chain FA, can never be a substrate of gluconeogenesis.



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 169-170

questions.stem: A genetic disorder renders fructose 1,6-bisphosphatase in the liver less sensitive to regulation by fructose 2,6-bisphosphate. All of the following metabolic changes occur EXCEPT:

options.label: A
options.text: Level of fructose 1,6-bisphosphate is higher than normal

options.label: B
options.text: Level of fructose 1,6-bisphosphate is lower than normal

questions.answerText: Level of fructose 1,6-bisphosphate is higher than normal
questions.solutionHtml:
Level of fructose 1,6-bisphosphate is higher than normal
  • Note that question is asking about the wrong statement. As shown in the flow chart below, the level of fructose 1,6 bisphosphate is lower than normal not higher in case of mutation. So, option A is wrong.
  • Normally Fructose 2,6-bisphosphate is the inhibitor of fructose 1,6 bisphosphatase (an enzyme of gluconeogenesis) and decreases the activity of fructose 1,6 bisphosphatase, Thus, decreasing the rate of gluconeogenesis and increases the rate of glycolysis.
  • But now due to mutation, the activity of fructose 1,6-bisphosphatase is not decreased. So, fructose 1,6-bisphosphatase will increase. So, its substrate (fructose 1, 6 bisphosphate) is decreased and not increased (option A is false and option B is true)




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 189, 190

questions.stem: Which of the following is true for TIGAR?
questions.solutionHtml:
All of the above

TIGAR is a protein produced in cancerous cells and operates as:

  • So, activation of TIGAR leads to decreased glycolysis by the decrease of its positive regulator fructose 2,6-Bisphosphate.
  • Cell replication does not occur due to low energy in the Cell
  • Cancer cells become dormant and repair process begins and the cell become normal
  • However, if the repair process does not begin for some reason, the cell is killed by apoptosis to prevent cancer.




Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 7th Edition, Page No. 321,322

questions.stem: The enzyme present in both glycolysis and gluconeogenesis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Phosphoglycerate kinase
  • Conversion of glucose to pyruvate is known as Glycolysis whereas conversion of pyruvate to glucose is known as Gluconeogenesis.

Enzymes that are present ONLY in Glycolysis

Enzymes that are present ONLY in Gluconeogenesis

1.      Pyruvate kinase (Option D)

2.      PFK-1 (Option A)

3.      Hexokinase / Glucokinase

2.      PEPCK (Option B)

Enzymes that are common in BOTH the pathways

2.      Aldolase A

questions.stem: A child of age 11 years suddenly expressed dizziness, sweating, cold clammy skin, and difficulty in breathing. He was taken to the physician. Upon examination, the liver was palpable and tender. Laboratory investigation revealed raised lactate and deficiency of glucose 6-phosphatase. Select the organ in which glucose 6-phosphatase is found?
questions.solutionHtml:
Kidneys and liver

Glucose 6-phosphatase is found in the liver and kidneys. This enzyme catalyzes the dephosphorylation of glucose 6-phosphate into free glucose molecules during gluconeogenesis. Its deficiency characterizes as glycogen storage disease type I. It is manifested as retarded growth, poor tolerance to fasting, and hepatomegaly due to surplus accumulation of glycogen in the liver




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 182
